questions.question: What is dissolved oxygen in water?
choices: The oxygen atoms chemically bonded within every water molecule
Only oxygen inside floating leaves
Oxygen gas present in the water and available to aquatic organisms
The salt content of seawater

questions.question: What is turbidity?
choices: Cloudiness caused by suspended particles
The acidity of water alone
The total amount of dissolved oxygen
The temperature of a stream

questions.question: What can conductivity measurements indicate about water?
choices: The exact identity of every dissolved substance
The complete absence of microbes
The concentration of suspended solids alone
The presence and amount of electrically conducting dissolved ions

questions.question: Which measurement tells whether a water sample is acidic or basic?
choices: Turbidity
pH
Dissolved oxygen
Flow speed

questions.question: What is a fecal-indicator organism used to assess?
choices: Possible contamination associated with fecal material
The exact concentration of every chemical pollutant
The temperature history of a stream
The total amount of dissolved oxygen

questions.question: What does biochemical oxygen demand estimate?
choices: The oxygen atoms bonded within water molecules
Oxygen used by organisms breaking down organic matter under specified conditions
The amount of oxygen released by all plants per hour
The total gas pressure above the water

questions.question: What is a baseline measurement in a water study?
choices: A guaranteed safe condition for all future comparisons
A measurement that must be taken only after a spill
A limit that automatically applies to every water use
A reference condition used for comparison

questions.question: Why does colder freshwater generally hold more dissolved oxygen at equilibrium than warmer freshwater under comparable conditions?
choices: Cold water cannot support organisms that use oxygen
Warm water contains no oxygen atoms
Gas solubility generally increases as temperature decreases
Temperature affects only turbidity, not gas solubility

questions.question: Why can high turbidity reduce aquatic plant growth?
choices: Suspended particles reduce light penetration
Higher turbidity always improves light penetration
Plants obtain all their growth energy from suspended sediment
Turbidity affects only the water's acidity

questions.question: Why can excess nitrate and phosphate be concerns in surface water?
choices: They always eliminate microbial activity
They remove all plant nutrients from the water
They can promote excessive algae and plant growth
Nutrients cannot be transported in surface runoff

questions.question: Why does clear water not prove it is safe to drink?
choices: All harmful contaminants must be visibly cloudy
Harmful microbes or dissolved substances may be present
Water clarity identifies all dissolved substances
Only the water's color determines drinking safety

questions.question: Why should sampling containers and procedures be standardized?
choices: Standardized containers remove every pollutant automatically
Different procedures cannot affect measured values
Using one procedure makes all water sources identical
Contamination or method differences can distort comparisons

questions.question: Why should a water-quality investigation record sampling time and location?
choices: One sample represents every future condition
Recording location replaces the need for water tests
Sampling time cannot affect an observed concentration
Conditions can vary across places and times

questions.question: How can very high organic waste input affect dissolved oxygen?
choices: Organic waste always raises oxygen concentrations
Microbial decomposition can consume more oxygen
Organic matter prevents microorganisms from growing
Oxygen is consumed only by fish, never by microbes

questions.question: Why are several water-quality parameters measured rather than only one?
choices: Every parameter describes exactly the same property
A pH reading identifies every possible contaminant
Different measurements reveal different aspects of water condition
More tests make measurement uncertainty vanish

questions.question: Two samples have equal temperature, but one has much higher conductivity. What is a reasonable inference?
choices: It likely has more or more conductive dissolved ions
It necessarily supports more aquatic animals
It is automatically safe to drink
It contains no dissolved ions

questions.question: A stream's dissolved oxygen falls after organic wastewater enters. Which explanation should be investigated?
choices: An increase in gas solubility caused by higher temperature
Microbial oxygen use during decomposition
The absence of all microbial oxygen use
Organic waste removing water's chemically bonded oxygen

questions.question: A river is muddy after heavy rain. Which measurement most directly describes its suspended-particle cloudiness?
choices: pH
Dissolved oxygen
Temperature
Turbidity

questions.question: A water sample meets one classroom pH target. Which conclusion is justified?
choices: Its pH meets that target, but other safety and quality questions remain
It is safe to drink without further testing
It contains no microorganisms
It contains no dissolved metals

questions.question: Repeated samples show a downstream nutrient increase during rainy periods. What hypothesis fits?
choices: Rain necessarily removes all nutrients
The samples prove one specific property owner caused it
Runoff may be carrying nutrients into the stream
Nutrients cannot move through a watershed
